title: Earth's Next Ice Age Started, Then Stopped
summary:
About 2,000 years ago, the remains of a huge sheet of ice in the Canadian Arctic began to grow again. Scientists think this slow growth may have been the start of Earth's next ice age. By the 1960s, warmer summers made the ice shrink instead of grow.

Scientists think global warming may have stopped a new ice age that was already starting. "It was just getting started, everything was normal, the next glaciation was about to happen, and yet it stopped," says Nicolas Young, a scientist at Columbia University.

Most of this ice sheet melted as the climate warmed. But one piece is still there: the Barnes Ice Cap, on Baffin Island in Canada. It is about the size of Delaware.

The Barnes Ice Cap is frozen right onto the rock below it, so it does not slide. Plants that were buried by the growing ice stayed in place for thousands of years. Since the ice cap began to melt in 1960, those old plants have slowly appeared. That tells them when the ice covered each spot.
why_it_matters: It shows that people can change the climate of the whole planet, even something as big as an ice age.
